features.summary: WebRender’s GPU layer was reorganized so its renderer can use different graphics backends through a cleaner, backend-neutral interface, while making resource handling, texture uploads, profiling, and shader management more reliable. Rendering quality and efficiency also improved through tighter image sampling, better clipping and gradient behavior, improved anti-aliasing in SWGL, safer text and picture-cache handling, and less work for invisible content. A new debugger workflow can edit and hot-reload shaders at runtime, with useful compile errors sent back to connected tools.

features.summary: Compositing and layers received reliability fixes across CSS zoom, process and pipeline tracking, browser-parent lifetime handling, and compositor assertions. Android WebGL can now use SharedSurface_AndroidHardwareBuffer, improving hardware-buffer sharing, while APZ (asynchronous panning and zooming) now handles overscroll animations and overscroll-behavior more consistently across fling handoffs. Instrumentation for SVG and blob images also makes image activity easier to measure and tune.

Font metrics and locking were simplified and made safer, while color-font palette allocation now fails gracefully instead of risking an out-of-memory crash. Platform-specific changes adjust Android font API usage and gate Skrifa font initialization behind a runtime preference.

These are internal improvements that should make 2D drawing code simpler and more efficient, with no intended visual change.

features.summary: WebGPU now recognizes more device limits for storage buffers and textures in vertex and fragment shader stages. It can also enable the clip-distances feature when the GPU reports support and correctly report float32-blendable, which allows certain 32-bit floating-point color targets to participate in blending. These changes help web content use supported GPU capabilities instead of being unnecessarily restricted.

features.summary: WebRender received broad rendering and architecture improvements: its GPU backend is now separated behind backend-neutral interfaces, making OpenGL, software rendering, and other backends easier to maintain and evolve. Rendering was also made more accurate and efficient through better visibility culling, device-space clipping and snapping, anti-aliasing, gradient and image fixes, and limits on oversized glyph rasterization. Developer tools gained shader hot reloading and a scene inspector, while new tests cover tricky gradients, clipping, filters, and compositor paths.

features.summary: Compositing and layers work improved scrolling, overscroll behavior, input routing, and process-to-process safety across WebRender, APZ (asynchronous panning and zooming), and compositor bridges. It also strengthened video and image handling, including HDR metadata, Wayland HDR playback, RTP video orientation for WebRTC, Android hardware buffers, DMABUF, and GPU texture recycling. These changes should make scrolling and media rendering more reliable across Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and Wayland, with several fixes aimed at preventing crashes, flashes, and incorrect colors.

features.summary: Firefox’s font system now uses the Skrifa font engine more broadly for FreeType metrics and glyph lookup, while adding support for more CSS font features and Fangsong and Kai families. Font data is protected more carefully against concurrent access and large color-font palettes now use fallible allocation, reducing the risk of crashes or wasted memory. Hardware video encoding and decoding checks were also tightened, including disabling hardware decoding on Linux when DMABUF is unavailable.

features.summary: Moz2D improved Canvas 2D drawing performance by recycling path builders and adding fast paths for lines and circles. Image-processing code also received SIMD and convolution optimizations, safer indexing and initialization, and better handling of SVG `feConvolveMatrix` filters. These changes reduce repeated allocations and improve reliability and speed for drawing and filtered images.

features.summary: OpenGL image transfer was updated to handle Android `ImageReader` and `AHardwareBuffer` surfaces, including safer synchronization while buffers change ownership. Firefox also stopped requesting an unavailable D3D9 ANGLE backend and disabled Android shared-surface paths that are incompatible with ANGLE. On Linux, VA-API video blits now copy only the actual content, helping avoid incorrect pixels around decoded frames.

features.summary: WebGPU now recognizes more device limits and optional features, including storage buffers and textures per shader stage, `clip-distances`, and `float32-blendable`. It also adds transient attachments and updates the `wgpu` implementation, while improving handling of GPU buffers, DXGI textures, and Vulkan-backed DMABUF textures. These changes let compatible hardware expose more WebGPU capabilities and make resource lifetime handling safer.

features.summary: The WebGPU backend bindings were updated to a newer `wgpu` revision and cleaned up with consistent Rust 2021 formatting. Windows instance creation is now treated as fallible instead of assumed to succeed, and shader compilation responses are handled more explicitly. This improves build consistency and avoids failures when the graphics backend cannot be initialized.

It also added handling for HDR BT2100PQ full-range NV12 video and clarified memory reporting, helping video and display paths work more efficiently and accurately.

The tests also now validate matrix attribute draw limits, remove the obsolete video-frame callback preference, and apply small tooling and expectation fixes so graphics regressions are easier to detect.

It also made process types more structured, removed an obsolete macOS crash-reporter thread workaround, and strengthened compositor IPC validation to reject conflicting live pipeline IDs.

The work also corrected an SSE4.2 configuration typo and clarified that nsRect can be copied trivially, helping the compiler generate more efficient and correct code.

Remote images now preserve their intrinsic aspect ratio by default, with an explicit stretch option, and an Android code-coverage test was excluded where it is not reliable.

JXL decoding now uses a dedicated thread pool, allowing expensive image work to run in parallel without blocking other browser activity.

features.summary: Image decoding now releases consumers waiting on a SourceBuffer outside the decoder mutex, so those notifications do not keep the internal lock held and can reduce contention during media or image data processing. A small C++ cleanup also removes an unnecessary inequality operator where it was not needed.

features.summary: Graphics test infrastructure got better memory tracking for partial texture uploads. This helps catch uninitialized GPU memory and upload mistakes earlier, improving confidence that the rendering pipeline stays correct even before user-facing features change.

features.summary: Virtual- and augmented-reality window names are now kept in UTF-16, the wide-character format expected by the relevant platform APIs. This improves compatibility for window titles containing non-ASCII characters.
